title: Boat Ride 🛥

body:
The golden morning sunshine greeted us as we boarded our canal boat, ready to see the fairy tale sights of Strasbourg float gently by from the water! The scene along the riverbanks was straight out of an impressionist painting, with weeping willows trailing into the water, vibrant flower planters spilling over every railing, and locals sitting peacefully with their feet dangling toward the rippling waves. Naturally, Mom took that as her personal cue to begin snapping dozens of photos a minute!

We slipped on our headsets to listen to the English audio tour as our boat glided smoothly down the canal. We learned that centuries ago, Strasbourg was famous for its massive leather tanning trade. The historic timbered houses were built with open, slatted attic roofs so the natural breeze could flow straight through and dry out the hanging animal hides!

Then the audio guide delivered the most jaw-dropping historical gossip ever: back in the medieval days, local residents tossed all their dirty buckets straight into the canal! Centuries of mess flowed right through these waters! That already gave me the ultimate ick, but right at that exact second, a teenager playing on the shore swung off a weeping willow branch and splashed face-first into the river! My jaw hit the floor, and I felt so hilariously horrified on his behalf!

As we cruised under the archways, pedestrians leaned over the bridges waving and snapping pictures of our boat. Being the natural star of the tour, I had to flash my best pageant smile for practically forty straight minutes while making sure my hair stayed flawless! My cheeks were completely exhausted from smiling, but securing a top-tier cameo in random tourists' vacation scrapbooks is an absolute necessity!

Before long, we reached an engineering marvel: a canal lock built to carry boats across a water level drop of 1.7 meters. The heavy iron gates sealed behind us, water gushed into the chamber, and we slowly rose higher and higher! You couldn't feel the lift beneath you, but watching the wet stone walls sink down as the boat rose was fascinating! Once the gates swung open ahead, we sailed into open water, greeted by elegant white swans and the sweetest little fluffy baby goslings paddling beside their mother!

Our guide also explained the rich blend of French and German heritage woven into every street corner. Strasbourg changed hands between nations so many times that the street signs and monuments share an impossible blend of both languages! French is tricky enough, but German feels like solving a tongue-twister puzzle, so we happily let the audio tour handle all the pronunciations! Gliding beneath ancient stone bridges while soft reflections of timbered houses danced along the water was pure bliss, leaving us completely enchanted by the endless charm of this historic city!
author: zarmina

title: A Day In Strasbourg 💐
excerpt: Today felt like stepping right into the pages of a fairy tale as we woke up for our very first day in Strasbourg! I was so eager to see if the city matched the dreamy photos online, full of rustic timber houses, winding cobblestone lanes,
body:
Today felt like stepping right into the pages of a fairy tale as we woke up for our very first day in Strasbourg! I was so eager to see if the city matched the dreamy photos online, full of rustic timber houses, winding cobblestone lanes, and romantic bridges draped in colorful blossoms over shimmering canals. Well, plot twist: not every single house is shaped like a storybook barn! That is straight-up fake news, people!

Everything else, though, was absolute magic. We were wondering how every single flower box stays so ridiculously luscious and healthy, and we actually uncovered the secret: a giant water tanker truck rumbles through town, and a dedicated worker carefully waters every single flower display by hand! That explains why the entire city looks like a living postcard!

We spent hours wandering along the charming stone streets and crossing picture-perfect bridges. Mom was snapping away on her camera going "click, click, click, click, click!" because everything was just too breathtaking for her eyes to handle!

Then we came across this grand historic building completely wrapped in cute white flowers. It looked stunning! Inside, we explored halls filled with elegant statues before making our way up to the wide rooftop terrace. Flowering vines tumbled down the sloping edges, and the viewpoint looked out over the quiet canal where graceful white swans drifted in the sunlight. Across the water stood three massive fortified stone towers standing guard over the river. There were originally four built to protect the waterway, but the fourth was destroyed during a war, leaving the defenses slightly open. Historic soldiers used to watch over the entire river right from inside them!

In the distance between the towers, the soaring, dark spire of the Strasbourg Cathedral pierced the sky. Mom was determined to reach the top for epic pictures, so naturally, we took on the challenge!

It was a climb of 330 spiral stone stairs. I was fully prepared for my legs to burn, but they barely even broke a sweat because the hiker in front of me moved at a leisurely snail's pace! I don't blame her since cathedral climbs are serious workouts, but I have conquered so many towers by now that I am practically a seasoned mountain climber! The intricate gothic carvings on the cathedral walls were unreal, and by pure luck, we stepped onto the balcony right as the giant historic bells began to ring! On our way back down, I spotted Beth perched high on a ledge, clearly scheming her next pigeon attack!

To celebrate conquering the heights, we headed over to a cozy Italian restaurant for a well-deserved dinner. We were the very first customers to walk through the doors, which felt a little funny, but before long, the whole dining room was buzzing with people! I ordered a gorgeous pasta bathed in a rich, velvety white sauce that tasted like the fanciest mac and cheese on earth. Our server brought over a dish of freshly grated parmesan, and I dumped every single crumb directly onto my pasta! It contained tiny mushrooms, but the sauce was so flavorful that I could barely taste them, which was a huge victory since I usually despise mushrooms! It was so creamy, savory, and completely scrumdiddlyumptious!

Ayana enjoyed a fresh margherita pizza, while Mom chose a delicious pizza and salad pairing. Ayana's pizza came topped with olives, so we promptly staged a rescue mission to pick off every last olive before they could contaminate the pristine cheese, because let's be totally real, who actually enjoys olives? All and all it was a great experience.

title: Groundbreaking News: Baby Pigeons Exist! 🤯
excerpt: Today we were in Colmar, and it was so fairy tale like! It was so cute. They had all these timber framed houses with big bundles of flowers everywhere, which is a lot like Strasbourg, where we are staying now. We were just taking a day tri
body:
Today we were in Colmar, and it was so fairy tale like! It was so cute. They had all these timber framed houses with big bundles of flowers everywhere, which is a lot like Strasbourg, where we are staying now. We were just taking a day trip so that we could see a few other things, learn some history, and enjoy the scenery.

I was looking closely at one of the houses, and then I saw a pigeon kissing another pigeon. I was like, "Wait, are those pigeons kissing? Is Beth kissing another pigeon?" I didn't know she had a man! But then I looked closer and realized it was a baby pigeon!

Can you even believe they exist? I swear, when we were in Edinburgh, our whole family had this massive debate about how none of us had ever seen a baby pigeon before. We thought they literally didn't exist and just spawned into the world looking like regular adult pigeons!

They actually look a little different. They don't have the full adult pigeon face yet, so I think their features change as they grow. But it was a literal baby pigeon! It is actually insane that they exist. I was staring at a real life baby pigeon! It was kind of cute, and our timing was impeccable. When we came back from my search for earrings, the baby pigeon was completely hidden and you couldn't see it anymore.

Later on, I was trying to come up with the ultimate name for the baby pigeon. I realized "Death" would be completely perfect! First of all, it rhymes with Beth. Second, it is her child. Third, since Beth is always trying to target me with poop, it just fits the dramatic vibe!

So to officially set the record straight: the baby pigeon is a boy, his name is Death, and he is definitely her baby, not her man.We literally made a groundbreaking scientific discovery today: baby pigeons are real! Spread the news!

title: Chaos: Cancelled Trains and No Place to Stay 🚂
excerpt: Today we were hopping on a train to get to London. The train right before ours was canceled, and this station is kind of known for trains just not showing up! We were a little nervous, but we thought everything would work out fine. Then,
body:
Today we were hopping on a train to get to London. The train right before ours was canceled, and this station is kind of known for trains just not showing up! We were a little nervous, but we thought everything would work out fine. Then, literally one minute later, our train got canceled too!

We had to sprint over to the customer assistance desk. We were definitely panicking because the next train leaving for London was in two minutes, which was not looking very promising! We waited in line for a couple of frantic minutes, but they managed to sort out our tickets. We grabbed our bags, ran toward the platforms, and asked the staff if we were in the right spot. They pointed us toward platform three on the far side, so we had to sprint all the way across to the other side of the station!

We finally reached our train, but we boarded on the end farthest from our assigned seats. We had tons of heavy luggage, and the aisles were totally packed with people trying to squeeze in and out. After about 15 minutes, the train actually started moving just as we reached our row! When we got there, we realized people were sitting in our spots, so we politely asked them to move. Because of all the earlier cancellations, the train was completely overbooked, and lots of people had to stand in the aisles for the entire three-hour ride! We were so relieved we actually had seats.

When we got to London, we met up with a couple of Papa's friends and enjoyed some really good food and sweets. Then it was time for our next leg from London to Paris on the Eurostar! The train travels through tunnels located under the English Channel, which is so cool!

Getting through the station was an obstacle course. The line was massive, then we had to wait in another long line for security, and then another line after that! By the time we made it to the waiting area, we had about 30 minutes to wait. Another train was delayed, so two full trainloads of passengers were trying to board at the exact same time. We managed to snag three seats to rest for a few minutes before boarding. Luckily, we had premium tickets with huge seats that reclined, great Wi-Fi, and plenty of space for our luggage. I listened to music the whole ride, ready to relax and finally enjoy arriving in Paris!

Travel chaos struck again, though! We found out our upcoming train to Strasbourg, our next destination, got canceled! Mom managed to book a backup bus, but it takes double the time and costs double the money. Now we have a six-hour bus ride ahead of us, but I looked up photos of Strasbourg and it looks super cute, so I think it will definitely be worth it!

To top it all off, right as our train pulled into Paris, our host messaged us saying the electricity had completely gone out at our apartment! We had no idea where we were going to sleep. When we arrived, they moved us to an alternate place with only one bedroom and a super uncomfortable pull-out couch instead of the two-bedroom place we booked, and they won't even be able to fix the power during our stay!

So many crazy, unlucky things happened today, but I am still super grateful we made it to Paris in one piece! I am crossing my fingers that our travel between Strasbourg, Paris, and Sardinia goes smoothly. Wish me luck!

body:
Today I was just harmlessly walking around, and next thing I know, a pigeon pooped right next to me! I let out a huge gasp of surprise, followed by a giant sigh of relief because my hair was totally fine! I knew it was Beth. For the rest of the walk, I kept looking up and constantly checking my hair. I knew she must have flown on top of our train and followed us all the way to Paris! She was definitely just jealous because we had family photos taken at the Eiffel Tower and she wasn't invited!

When we arrived at the Eiffel Tower, there were around ten different wedding photo shoots happening! There were so many people there even though it was only eight in the morning. I got some stunning photos of myself, and everything looked perfect!

Afterward, we got a little treat: a French flan! It had a pastry crust with custard inside, and the top was baked to give it a nice golden layer. The inside was super creamy and gooey. It was really good, but I honestly would have liked a little more crust because there was almost too much custard!

When we headed back toward the Eiffel Tower to go home, it was barely visible compared to an hour earlier because all the clouds had rolled in. It was so fun taking family photos, even though we had to wake up super early!

title: The multi-train fiasco 🚊
excerpt: Yesterday we were at the train station, and we had no idea what to do because our train was canceled. So we went to these people, and they were like, "Okay, yeah, so you have to go get on the train, and we got you these seats." We asked
body:
Yesterday we were at the train station, and we had no idea what to do because our train was canceled. So we went to these people, and they were like, "Okay, yeah, so you have to go get on the train, and we got you these seats." We asked another person because we had no idea which side we were on. Then we had to run to the other side because we were on the wrong side.

We waited for like 10 seconds when we got there, the train arrived, and we ran to get our seats. But there was a huge block up, so all we did was stand there until the train started. It took a really long time for people to move. Finally, we got to our seats and put away our suitcases in the luggage thing. We found that people were sitting in our seats! Zarmina and I sat down in our seats because the people there quickly moved. In Mommy's and Puppy's seats, the people were like, "Oh yeah, these are our seats." We were like, "Okay, yeah, but they said they were available." It took them a little bit, but finally they got their seats.

After we got off of that train, which took a very long time—and I got bored, and I read, and I was absolutely starving—we went to the next train station to go to Paris. We had just gone to London, King's Cross. That's where the Harry Potter thing took place. So I said we have to see Platform 9 3/4. We went to see Platform 9 3/4 because we had quite a while, and I took a photo there. It was a lot of fun, but the line was mega long!

We went to get some food, and Puppy heard his name get called. He saw some friends who had just been there for a few days, and he spotted them out of everybody! Her kids were around our age. We went down to this marketplace and looked at some food. Zarmina and I just decided to get some arepas, and Mom was going to get some Korean chicken thing. We went up and ate, and it was delicious. We met another one of Puppy's friends named Saima. They talked for a while. I got bored, I read, I was exhausted.

It was finally time for us to go, and we went to the other train place. They said, "Oh yeah, you have to wait like 20 more minutes until it opens." Zarmina and I just went into the store and browsed for a bit, found this fidget, and just kept playing with it. Then Mom said, "We have to go."

We went over, and the line was the longest thing I've ever seen in my life. It was like an airport, but the line actually moved pretty quickly. We went around and around and around and around and around and around! Finally, we got to the end, and then we had to go through another line to go through a thing where you went to another line where you had to go to a waiting space to wait for the train. I was like, "These are so many people." Zarmina said, "Oh yeah, maybe it's just one big train." It would have to be the size of an airport if it could fit that many people.

We finally got on the train, and it was actually really nice. The seats were nice, and we didn't have any problems getting into them. We were just going to wait a long time. Mom showed us a video about what Paris was like yesterday. It was this major thunderstorm with things flying everywhere and stuff. When we were on the train, it was only raining a bit, just sprinkling outside, but nothing more. Once I finished my book, I got bored and started to read another book.

Once we finally got off, we got to Paris. We took the underground, but first we had to get the ticket things. There was this loud music playing, and it was really annoying. Even when it wasn't someone playing it, it was coming from the ceilings and it was so loud. It was really annoying and hard for people to focus.

We got to the apartment, and there were troubles with the apartment, so we had to stay in a different room on the second floor, but it was okay. It was basically the same except minus one room, which is annoying because I had to sleep on a fold-out couch. But the plus of coming here was I get to see my friend, Bea!

We saw the Eiffel Tower, took photos, and there was this flashing stuff. Mom texted Dan, her friend, and he said, "Oh, I wonder if that's everybody taking flash photos, like flash, flash, flash, flash, flash!" I thought it only happened that time, and then later it happened at 10:01 because we stayed up really late. We were like, "Oh, yeah, it's always like 5 minutes every hour."

Bea had a dog named Aussie. We pet Aussie, got some ice cream, took some photos, and had fun. So yeah. It was really fun, but annoying because of the train stuff. But overall, you should check out Platform 9 3/4 if you like Harry Potter and are okay with standing in long lines!
author: ayana

title: Chocolate, Chocolate and More Chocolate!! 🍫
excerpt: Today we went to a chocolate museum! When we walked in, the smell hit me straight in the face: chocolate! I knew we just had to get some. I begged Mom for 10 straight minutes until our tour began, but she didn't give in! I was even dramat
body:
Today we went to a chocolate museum! When we walked in, the smell hit me straight in the face: chocolate! I knew we just had to get some. I begged Mom for 10 straight minutes until our tour began, but she didn't give in! I was even dramatic about it. Like how did she not get chocolate?

The tour ended up being really cool. First, we talked about our favorite chocolates, and we got a sample. It wasn't very good because it was dark chocolate. Gross!

Then we learned how chocolate came to be. It started with cocoa beans from the Americas that were brought back to Europe. Ancient rulers believed chocolate gave them a longer lifespan and made them stronger, so the Aztec king supposedly drank around 50 cups a day! Back then they didn't make chocolate with sugar, so it was basically watery, bitter, spicy dark chocolate. It gave me such an ick!

Next, we learned about the famous York chocolate families, especially the Rowntree family, who created famous treats like the KitKat right here in York! And yes, we got a KitKat to sample!

Then we learned the whole process of how chocolate is made. First, we crushed up the cocoa nibs from the roasted beans and tried them. It tasted like crunchy, bitter little bits of chopped-up unsweetened chocolate. Next, they use a pressing machine that separates the cocoa butter from the cocoa solids, which turn into cocoa powder. Then they mix the ingredients back together in exact ratios so the consistency turns out totally smooth.

We tried 100% pure dark chocolate, and it tasted so gross! It was sour, bitter, and slightly spicy. It was truly disgusting! Nowadays, they mix in sugar. A bar with 55% cocoa has a good amount of sweetness, and we got to sample that one, which was actually pretty good. For milk chocolate, you can't just pour in liquid milk or it would ruin the texture, so they blend in powdered milk instead. That gives it that smooth, creamy taste and lighter color, which I love!

We also learned that white chocolate is made purely from cocoa butter. Even though some people say it isn't real chocolate, it totally is because it comes directly from the cocoa bean!

After that, we made our own chocolate lollipops! We spread warm white chocolate in a big circle and topped it with gummies, salted caramel crisps, and sprinkles. Mine looked a little chaotic, but it tasted delicious, especially with the gummies!

Next, we watched a chocolatier demonstrate how filled chocolates are made. First, he poured melted chocolate into molds, tapped out all the air bubbles, scraped off the excess, and tipped it upside down so only a thin outer shell remained. Once that set, he piped in a mango filling, topped it with another layer of chocolate to seal the bottom, and popped it into the chiller. He gave us a fresh batch to try, and the mango chocolate was amazing! The bottom layer was a little thicker than the top shell, but the flavor was incredible.

In the end, my begging totally paid off because Mom let us buy a giant haul of chocolate! We got a 12-piece gift box for family, a 12-piece box for ourselves, four chocolate bars, a special treat for Mom, and a few extra goodies. We ended up with so much chocolate! It was totally worth it. The chocolate was amazing quality, and I would definitely recommend visiting!

title: The chocolate adventure🍫
excerpt: I wasn't expecting the re to be so many samples of chocolate, so I was begging Mom to get chocolate. When we went in, we got one of the first types of chocolate that was ever there. It was really bitter and really dark chocolatey, and I did
body:
I wasn't expecting the re to be so many samples of chocolate, so I was begging Mom to get chocolate. When we went in, we got one of the first types of chocolate that was ever there. It was really bitter and really dark chocolatey, and I didn't like it.

Then we went into the next room, and it was telling all about the history of chocolate and this man who drank 50 cups a day of this hot chocolate thing. Okay, so it's the exact opposite of hot chocolate. It's bitter and cold. When I tried it, it was absolutely disgusting. It was freezing! It was basically melted dark chocolate that tasted like chocolate water. They showed us how they made the chocolate stuff, all these things, and what type of chocolates they made.

In York, that's where Kit Kats were invented. We got to have some of these types of candies. I liked mine the best, Puppy liked his the best, Mom liked hers the best, and Zarmina liked hers the best. No one liked each other's! They just liked the one that they chose, which was good. All the chocolates looked so delicious because there were like 11 different types.

Then we went on to the next room, and it was about Kit Kats and stuff like that. There was this dude who had to make Kit Kats in hot weather a really long time ago. Since there was no air conditioning, they had to open the window, and wasps came in. So this dude had the job of swatting away the wasps. If they got into the chocolate, he had to swat them out. We all got a Kit Kat. Puppy had a feeling there was going to be a lot of chocolate on this tour, and there was. It was like millions. Every time we went into a new room, there was more chocolate!

We went downstairs, and the dude started talking about making chocolate and how there are several different processes. We had 100% chocolate, and it was so bad, like disgusting! I took one taste of it, one lick, a bite, and then I spit it out in the trash. It was absolutely disgusting. I would never have that again. It's way too dark. After that, we had some normal dark chocolate, like 50% dark chocolate.

He said that he needed to set this thing up for about 5 seconds. We went over there and got into groups with these plastic bags on a tray. There were two plastic bags on each tray, and we were supposed to write our name on one side of the plastic bag and put it facing the tray. The dude came around with white chocolate and put a dollop on ours to make lollies. We took one of the little things that you hold it with and put it in, and then we put all our toppings in. My favorite was this gummy. It was so good. I ate some at first, and it was so yummy. I loved it.

After that, this guy filled chocolate molds. First, he scooped up all the chocolate and put it inside of there. It looked so good. He cleared it so that it was just the molds, waited for a few seconds, and tapped it to make sure that it wasn't fully solid, but mostly. He flipped it upside down because he was just doing an outer layer. All the chocolate came out, and it was so satisfying! He scraped off all the excess chocolate and waited for the mold to dry upside down. He had another one ready so we didn't have to wait. It already had a mango thing inside of it, so he just had to top it with some chocolate. Once they were finished, we ate them, and they were delicious.

Then we got our lollies back. The favorite part of mine was the gummy. I didn't really like the rest of it, so yeah.

If you are in York, you should definitely check it out. It was so much fun!

title: An Adventure Awaits! 🐈‍⬛
excerpt: Today we went on a hike to see this crater! It was really beautiful with all these different colors: purples, reds, oranges, greens, yellows, and the bright blue sky that complemented it all. It looked so pretty with so many lively plants
body:
Today we went on a hike to see this crater! It was really beautiful with all these different colors: purples, reds, oranges, greens, yellows, and the bright blue sky that complemented it all. It looked so pretty with so many lively plants everywhere!

As we walked on the trail, we saw some sheepies. There were five of them, and I loved this one that was just a giant ball of fluff! It looked kind of fat, but it was still really cute. There was another one with a super wide face, one that was really skinny, and two others that were total besties always hanging out together. Later on our way back, I realized the fluffy sheepy I liked the most was actually a baby because it went over to nurse from its mom, who turned out to be the really skinny one! It was so cute, and definitely still my favorite.

We wanted to hike down into the crater area that was covered in greenery. The trail was pretty steep, and I was basically rolling down like a bowling ball, but the view was gorgeous! Down there, we saw even more sheepies that looked like they were playing an intense game of hide-and-seek. One sheep was totally the seeker, another was hiding behind a tree, two were chilling on the ground, one was by a tree further away, and one was hidden deep in the ferns all the way across the field. I knew that fern sheep was never going to get found! I couldn't stay to watch the whole game, but I could tell the seeker was definitely about to find the one behind the nearest tree.

Our next stop was getting food. I ordered an egg and mayo sandwich with salad, and we ate lemon cakes! The lemon cake was so good. I loved the cake part even more than the frosting, but the whole thing was still scrum-diddly-umptious!

While we were there, I met a kitty named Beauty. She was beautiful, obviously, just like her name! She was black and white with the biggest green eyes. I felt kind of bad for her though because she had scratches and ticks. There was another calico cat nearby that had a swollen eye and battle wounds, so they didn't look completely well. But then I realized they might have gotten into a fight with prey because Ayana spotted a bird wing on the ground, and then we found the other wing later! They were probably out hunting, but they were still super cute.

Next, we went on a short walk because Mom wanted to take photos of some houses. We saw another gorgeous cat with gray stripes and a white face, but it ran away pretty quickly, so it was probably a local pet.

Finally, we drove up to these amazing castle ruins! The drive was beautiful, all the heather was blooming. So there were fields of purple with white dotted around (sheep). It was so pretty, and we climbed all the way to the top and walked all around the walls. But as I was sliding down a slope, my knee brushed against this stinging nettle plant that pricked me. You couldn't even see the scratch at first, but it stung so bad! When I got back into the car, three blistery bubbles popped up on my knee, and it turned super red and painful. Eventually the reaction faded away, but like, come on plants, be nicer!

We took a stop so Mom could take photos of us (Ayana and me). We posed and got deep into the heather, but the light was too bright (rare) so, Mom had trouble taking photos that complimented the purple. I even got to make a throne out of the heather by laying on it (which didn't damage the plants). Anyway, I had loads of fun, ate great food, and I can't wait to eat more food!
author: zarmina

title: The hike and we saw another cat 🐈

Today we went on a hike, and when we got there, we went to the map thing. There was a story where a giant named Wade got angry at his wife and picked up handfuls of earth and threw them. He missed, and that's what made the gigantic hole in the ground.

We started to walk. A few minutes later, we heard some sheepies, and they were adorable. We kept walking and seeing a little more sheepies. One of them was cute and was trying to drink from its mother. It was really small, and it looked fatter than the mom because it had more fur on it. The mom looked like she'd been sheared, but all the sheepies were in pretty good shape. Their fur was looking nice, and just walking around, they weren't too afraid of us.

Then we saw these people on the trail. Since we were going away from the hole where we wanted to take photos, they were like, "Oh yeah, it's a 4-mile, 4-hour hike, and there's a different way where you can go down to the hole." So we went that way. It was pretty steep the way Zarmina, Puppy, and I went. But Mom went a different way that was probably as steep but easier because there weren't crumbling rocks.

We went down and down, and we had to hurry up because our parking time would end soon. We saw a couple more sheepies. When Puppy and I were ahead of Mom and Zarmina, I saw these two sheepies that looked exactly the same. They were twins, and they were really small, trailing this older sheep that looked like their mother.

Once we got back in the car, we turned on the AC because it was very hard to hike all the way back up. We were going to stop and go to this lunch place. On the way, I saw a few pregnant sheepies. Or what I thought were pregnant sheepies because they were way wider, like a lot, a lot wider around the stomach area.

We went to the cute little town. We saw all these adorable houses, and when we got there, we parked. Zarmina and I saw this adorable kitty. We wanted to jump over this fence thing and pet it, but we knew that we shouldn't do that. We went into the cafe where the kitty was outside of. We were like, "Oh, we saw the kitty outside. Whose is it?" He was like, "Oh yeah, that's mine." Then they were like, "Oh, I also have another kitty who's like downstairs somewhere." We were like, "Okay."

Quickly after we ordered, Zarmina and I went to see the kitty. After petting the cute, adorable kitty that was black and white, we looked for the other one. We found it, but it was outside of the fence thing just chilling, probably not wanting to be touched. So Zarmina and I left it alone. It also looked kind of sick or hurt. We washed our hands and ate some foods.

It took Zarmina and I a really long time to say goodbye. Mom was like, "Oh yeah, we're going to be coming back." We just went on a quick walk to take a photo of some of the houses that Mom saw on our way in and went to this church. It said it was open, but it was completely empty. It was also very small.

Then we took the car, and we were going to drive up to this little thing that Mom wanted to take photos of. We had to drive in the car because it was a few minutes away. The fields of heather were crazy! It was purple spread out like a blanket. We saw a lot of sheepies, and a sign said, "Slow down, sheepies." Another one said, "Slow, a lamb was killed here." I was like, "Aw, a lamb was killed here. That's really sad." Or they could just be cautioning us to make sure that we don't kill any lambs or anything like that.

After we got there, there were these ruins that were arches, and Zarmina and I climbed on top of them while Puppy went to the very top. It actually wasn't that much of a climb. It was just more of a walking uphill thing. We sat on the edge, and Mom took photos of us. Then we went up where Puppy was, and Mom took more photos of us. About a billion photos later, we went down, and it was really scary because we were high above the ground.

We walked back to the car, and Mom wanted to take photos of Zarmina and I in the heather. So we parked on the side after we got to a lot of heather. Mom wanted us to go farther into this place, and I just loved running in the heather. Then Mom said that the sun wasn't sunning. So we went to a different spot, and the heather felt much nicer. The ground was actually soft, the heather was taller, and there were trees in the background, so it made a nice contrast with the purple of the heather. Zarmina and I posed for Mom, and at the end, we just decided to lay down because it felt so nice. There was moss all over it.

After that, we went back. If you go to York, you should definitely check it out!

title: The world biggest fossilied poop 💩
excerpt: Today we went to a Viking museum. We walked in, and we learned they were going to tell us about a fossilized poo, and that really got me interested! At the end, the tour person asked if we had any questions, so I asked about the fossilize
body:
Today we went to a Viking museum. We walked in, and we learned they were going to tell us about a fossilized poo, and that really got me interested! At the end, the tour person asked if we had any questions, so I asked about the fossilized poo.

He was like, "Yeah, it's the biggest fossilized poo there ever was because back when the Vikings were in York, they had worms in their stomach." Most people have one or two worms, but this man had hundreds, millions of worms in his stomach, and he had two different types of worms. They clipped off the instinct for the brain so that it would never be full. So he just kept eating and eating and eating and eating!

But 95% of it was bread, and the rest of it was meats. Since they didn't have salt—well, they did, but it was really expensive, and they didn't want to use it on preserving meats—their meats got all spoiled and rotten even though they tried to preserve it.

It was just found in a tin underground, which would probably have been in a ditch or something. Then they said that the poo earned its place in the Guinness World Record Book for largest fossilized poo! It also was way bigger than it is now because some of it just shrunk being fossilized.

You should definitely check out the museum. Seeing the poo was really fun!

title: A Viking: Poop, Teeth and Much More 💩😁
excerpt: Today we went on a Viking tour, and as soon as you go down the stairs, the smell hits you straight in the face! It was like a mix of pee and stale bread. It was so horrible that I breathed through my mouth instead of my nose the entire ti
body:
Today we went on a Viking tour, and as soon as you go down the stairs, the smell hits you straight in the face! It was like a mix of pee and stale bread. It was so horrible that I breathed through my mouth instead of my nose the entire time!

First, we saw the remains of ancient Viking houses. There was glass over the excavated ground so you could step right over it and see the foundations. When our tour guide came, he explained that the houses were built out of clay, sticks, and horse manure, which didn't last very long. Since York is situated between two rivers, the ground was super marshy. The houses would sink down, and people would just build new houses right on top of the old ones again and again, leaving all these layers preserved underground!

Next, we got in line to ride in these little moving ride cars. At first, there was just a screen showing a video, and I thought it was going to be boring. But as we rode deeper in, actual life-size Viking scenes appeared all around us! They used animatronic technology to make the figures move their arms, work, and talk. We saw a craftsman carving wooden animals, regular village houses, cats, dogs, and tons of birds. It showed exactly what daily life was like back in the 900s, and it was so cool to see!

After the ride, we went to look at the skeletal remains. There were three skeletons on display. One skeleton had really nice teeth (on the left), and even though they were worn down, the bite was still totally aligned! Another had teeth falling out everywhere, and the third had a sideways bite with only a few teeth left. These were around a thousand years old, so it was wild to see how well the bones survived! One skeleton had a very defined face where you could clearly see the nose cavity and eye sockets, while another had a broken, scrunched skull. It was crazy to see what we might look like a thousand years from now!

Then we saw the world's largest fossilized poop! It is literally in the Guinness World Records. This Viking man created it because his diet consisted mostly of bread and meat. Back then, they could not preserve meat properly, so people often ate spoiled meat containing parasites. The worms in his system interfered with his digestion, so he would just keep eating without feeling full! Eventually, he produced this massive specimen, which is still huge today even though it has dried down to about a third of its original size

After that, we looked at artifacts and asked questions. There were furs, jewelry, and a skinny, woven trap used for catching eels in the shallow river. We also learned that Vikings were actually much cleaner than people think! They used fine-toothed combs to get lice and nits out of their hair, and they bathed once a week, compared to others who only bathed once or twice a year. The fanciest combs were carved directly from shed deer antlers. It was so neat looking at real combs, jewelry, and tools from the 900s. I had a blast and would totally recommend checking it out!

title: The Massive Minster⛪
excerpt: Today we went to the Minster, and it was huge! From the outside, it looked gigantic. The architects designed it so all the weight was supported on the outside, which is how they were able to make such massive windows without the building co
body:
Today we went to the Minster, and it was huge! From the outside, it looked gigantic. The architects designed it so all the weight was supported on the outside, which is how they were able to make such massive windows without the building collapsing. Everything just fit together so nicely!

When you actually went inside and looked up, the ceilings were way more than 20 feet high, they were absolutely massive! You look up and see all of these golden plates and cool architectural details. The stained glass is insanely beautiful. It is made of thousands of tiny little glass pieces that create this giant artwork, and there are so many different windows everywhere. There are also statues of all the kings, and you discover so many little hidden details as you walk through.

We had such an amazing guide who explained how everything fit together! There was this one special room we went into that was mostly stained glass all around, built in an octagonal, angled shape. It was one of those rooms where sound bounces across the walls, so Ayana and I tested it from opposite sides, and we could hear each other whispering perfectly!

When we walked back into the main nave, a priest was giving a prayer. Even with a microphone, his voice echoed and projected so powerfully across the giant stone walls. The acoustics in there were incredible!

We also learned how the Minster evolved from a tiny little structure into this huge, massive cathedral over hundreds of years. They constantly have to restore and rebuild parts of it because the stone they used is very soft and crumbles over time. During wartime, they even had to carefully take out all the precious stained glass windows and hide them so bombs wouldn't shatter them!

Even though the building is ginormous, historically people only came here once or twice a year for major festivals, which seems wild for a place so big! Now you can visit the museum area to see the stained glass up close and watch the light reflect all different colors. Up near the high walls, you can spot the heraldic shields of the wealthy families who donated money to build the cathedral. Our guide explained that stained glass was ridiculously expensive back then: clear glass was the cheapest, blue was super expensive, and purple was the rarest and most expensive of all! It was so cool getting to see all the history and explore such a massive place!

A few days ago, I went to this shop called The Weird Shop, and I saw this duck. It really caught my eye. I was just like, "Oh my god, that's really cute." It caught my eye because a few days earlier, I went to this place called The King's Wark. It was full of ducks and had hidden ducks all over! So it made me think of them, and I was like, "Oh, I should bring that duck to them."

It was a black duck, so it would be easier to hide than the normal yellow ducks. It was like a small plastic figurine. I got it, and Mommy and Puppy had no idea what I was doing. They were like, "Okay, she's getting a duck."

A few days later, I was walking close to the King's Wark, and I decided to just drop off the duck when we went there. I walked in, and there was barely anybody there. The worker who had told us that this person hid yellow ducks everywhere in the King's Wark was there—Zarmina and I had found about 20!

I was like, "Okay, now I'm going to just put this duck somewhere." They were like, "Oh my god, really?" They thought I was just showing them the duck, but no, I was actually giving it to them. Then they got me some white glue thing that looks kind of like clay, and they put it on the bottom of my duck. Zarmina and I had to find a place to put it.

It took us a while to find the place, but we finally decided on a spot near where we first sat at the King's Wark. It was on the fireplace, and it blended in with the wall, so it would be hard to find. The people behind the counter were so excited. They were like, "Oh my god, that's amazing!"

Then the craziest thing happened. Some people had just paid them in US dollars instead of pounds, so they gave us each $20! Zarmina got $20, and I got $20. On top of that, they also gave us both a KitKat. It was crazy. I still cannot get over it. It was so nice of them.

If you come to Edinburgh, you should definitely check out the King's Wark!

title: Exploring Mary King's Close
excerpt: Today we went on a tour of The Real Mary King's Close! Our tour guide was 200 years old! Not really, but she was showing us how life looked back in her time. The first thing she showed us was all about why it's called Mary King's Close. Th
body:
Today we went on a tour of The Real Mary King's Close! Our tour guide was 200 years old! Not really, but she was showing us how life looked back in her time. The first thing she showed us was all about why it's called Mary King's Close. There was this woman called Mary King who ran these markets and was pretty well known, but her husband died so she had to take over. At the time, 45% of the households in Mary King's Close were headed by women, which was a huge achievement for women back in the day! They don't know the exact reason it was named after her, but those were definitely some of the main reasons.

Then we went to learn about the plague and how there were 11 different outbreaks! The worst one was the last one, the pneumonic plague, where you would die within 48 hours of getting symptoms, with only a 5% chance of making it!

Then there was the bubonic plague, where you would get these welts that would swell to the size of your fist. The plague doctor was able to treat this one by draining out all the pus and putting some ointment on it to help with healing, but then they would have to take a burning hot iron and seal the welts shut! It was a very painful treatment, though it did work and gave you a 50% chance of survival.

Of course, all of these plagues were passed by the fleas on rats. Because families lived so close together with so many people crammed into one house, the youngest person would take out the waste bucket and go down the street to throw out all the pee and poop. All of that waste attracted the rats, which had the fleas that spread the plague to humans! People back then didn't know it was rodents causing it, they thought there were little demons in the air cursing people!

The doctor was covered in leather from head to toe and had this raven shaped beak stuffed with sweet smelling flowers to act like an air filter, plus a special hat so people knew he was a doctor. There was this doctor named George who went around treating people, but because the government was so focused on trying to stop the plague, they didn't have enough funds to pay him. After 10 years of legal fighting, he finally got one payment, and then he died six weeks later!

Next, we were able to go see a bigger house where a family actually had three whole rooms, which was a lot for back then! Then we went to see our tour guide's husband's setup. He had a thunderbox, which was an early toilet, and he was so proud of this design that he would open all the doors in the house! When people were walking up and down the close, they could see him using it and know that it was a real toilet, so he was totally showing off!

It was really cool learning about all these different things and how people lived back in the day. Our tour guide was great and she explained everything perfectly! We later found out she lied to us and that she wasn't actually 200 years old, which is so sad! Anyways, I had loads of fun!

title: The frog Loch 🐸
excerpt: Today we went on a hike to a loch. We needed to take up some time, so we decided to go on a hike on another loch because we were going to do a border collie thing in one hour.
body:
Today we went on a hike to a loch. We needed to take up some time, so we decided to go on a hike on another loch because we were going to do a border collie thing in one hour. We were following this car because I think they were going to the loch too. Mommy and Puppy were worrying about parking, even though when we got there, only two cars were there. We were like, "Oh, well, we didn't need to worry about that."

There was a map, and because the internet was bad, we just looked at the map and we were like, "Okay, so we're going to go on the white trail around the loch." A few minutes in, Zarmina saw a frog and she was like, "Aw, a frog." Mom was like, "Yeah, there are like thousands of frogs on this loch." So, we saw a lot of frogs. Mom saw a great place to take some photos, and she took a bunch of amazing photos.

It was off the path, so Puppy, Zarmina, and I decided to just go on this other path back to the trail. We thought it was a path, but it wasn't actually a path. It was just like this overgrown thing that kind of looked like a path at the start. It took us a little bit. We told Mom not to follow us after we were off the trail, but Mom had already started to follow us, and she didn't know where we were. So, I jumped into the bushes, and I found her, and then I led her back the way that I came. There was a lot of moss on the ground, so it was really squishy.

Once we were back on the trail, we kept following the white trail, and we saw a lot more froggies. Then we saw this beetle, and we were like, "Aw, it's flipped over." So, we flipped it the correct way with a leaf. It fell back onto its back again, so we flipped it over again. We were like, "Okay, we'll come back this way again, so if it's flipped over, we can save it again."

We kept walking for a little bit longer, then we came across fields of heather. It was so pretty! It was completely purple, and Mom was like, "Oh my god, I have to take a photo of you guys." So we didn't have to step on it because it was really boggy, there was like a wood thing going across it so that we could just walk on that. Zarmina and I jumped off it and went into the heather, and Mom took a few photos of us.

After that, the landscape changed and it turned into long reeds. It was still boggy, so the wood thing was still there. Then we kept walking and we followed the white markings where the cars could also go down, but we didn't see any. Then Zarmina thought that a frog had jumped under her foot and she had stepped on it, but I didn't think it was a frog. We had to decide which way to go. We were going in a circle and we had a few confusion moments where we were like, "Wait, are we going that way?"

Then we finally went back to the trail where we started, and we saw the beetle again. It was flipped over. So this time we helped it get to the side—well, Puppy did. He helped it get to the side of the trail and flipped it over so that it could walk properly.

We finished the hike and we still had some time, so we just decided to eat some food. You should try out that hike. It's really fun. The froggies are also super cute!

body:

title: Ceilidh and New Friends 🕺

body:
Today we went to a ceilidh, which is a Scottish barn dance! From the moment I walked in, I saw this girl who had such a cute fit and was practically the only girl that looked near my age. I observed the first dance and was very grateful that there was a person leading it, telling us the steps on how to do the dancing. So I jumped onto the dance floor, ready to dance, totally not expecting what was about to come!

We got into groups of four and you would do these dances. For me, I'm a very simplistic person, so it felt very overcomplicated! I somehow managed to squeeze in between people because everyone was so packed together that if one person went over, you would go flying across the room. It was literally a domino effect! Everybody was trying to squeeze around each other to do the dance on the beat, but it was so hard because everybody had to move so quickly in such a little amount of space. As my hair was flying around and my body was moving in places it wasn't meant to be going, I was trying to make myself my tiniest self while spinning around in circles. Finally, the dance stopped. I was parched, so I grabbed some water and waited until the next dance!

So we were doing our own dance thing, and remember what I said about dominoes? Well, we were doing a dance where you're meant to bend down so that people can run in between you. The person in front of me fell right on top of me! I lost my balance and fell, with my hair landing everywhere and getting dirty on the floor! I was very mad about my hair, but the bruises were on a whole different level. That would ruin my beautifully moisturized body, like I put a lot of effort into this!

Anyway, the dancing was loads of fun! I got totally dizzy and almost fell over, which was really fun. My hair was plastered across my face, which was not very fun!

Anyway, I loved doing it. At the very end, the girl who I saw at the beginning came up to me and asked if I wanted to dance with her because there was music playing, so we were just vibing and dancing together. It was really fun!

title: Perfect Pink Nails 💅
excerpt: Today we went to get our nails done! I knew I wanted a pink, but which color? There were like billions to choose from! After hours of searching, I found the right color. As I was picking out the color, I couldn't wait to see how it looked.
body:
Today we went to get our nails done!

I knew I wanted a pink, but which color?

There were like billions to choose from!

After hours of searching, I found the right color.

As I was picking out the color, I couldn't wait to see how it looked.

They had a whole process for the nails.

First, they file down your nails into perfect almond shapes, and then they use this tool that takes off the top part of your nails to make it a flatter surface to put the gel on.

Then he did like five coats!

He first did a regular clear coat.

Then he did pink, and then he did pink again, and then he did pink again, and then he did pink again just to make sure it was perfect!

After that, I think he put on a clear coat to make sure it set on my nails.

Now, every time I touch them, they just feel so silky, and I love my nails!

It was really fun getting them done!

body:
Today we were walking to a friend's house, and out of nowhere, a pigeon pooped! Luckily I was fast enough to yeet myself out of the way. The pigeon practically pooped on my head, like on my beautiful hair! How could Beth do this to me? This is why you cover your head and let your instincts take over. Take notes!

Then, as I was walking, a random bug flew straight into my face! Like, mind your manners! I felt so offended that a bug could fly into my face. It was such a horrible experience! Imagine a bug flying straight into your chin. Are they trying to prove a point or something? So rude. So rude!

Anyway, after that we went to the ceilidh where we did some dancing, and we saw this really cool performance! We came in right in the middle of it. There were people fighting with swords, and there was this guy going up a huge pole that six people were holding up with their body weight. As he went up, he was doing all these cool moves, sliding back and forth and down, and it was super fun!

When he got to the top, he was also going to be the princess. So after this woman passed him his torches, where he lit them on fire and spun them around in a circle, he extinguished them. He took off his shirt where he had a bra underneath, and another person tossed up a wig. He put the pink wig on his head, and then he was able to slide all the way down to the bottom of the pole, stopping just before banging his head on the ground!

He kept shouting, "Ed in bra! Ed in bra!" which was really funny because if you say it all together, it sounds like Edinburgh, the town that we're in! It was so fun, and I think it was one of the best street performances I've ever seen!

title: The Car Key Crisis 🔑
excerpt: Today we drove to return the car, and the instructions told us to open the window barely, lock the car with the key, and then throw the key through the window. Papa first tried it, but it didn't lock, but the second time he tried, it worked
body:
Today we drove to return the car, and the instructions told us to open the window barely, lock the car with the key, and then throw the key through the window. Papa first tried it, but it didn't lock, but the second time he tried, it worked!

Just as he threw the keys in, while they were literally mid-air, he realized that his backpack was still inside along with all the food, his water bottle, and his iPad! The company said the other set of keys would be mailed to the place we were staying at, but we were four hours away by train and we were dropping off the car to go to that exact place!

So we tried using a charging cord to bring the keys closer, but it needed a hook. Then we tried Mom's workout band, but it wasn't firm enough. After about 50 minutes of trying new things and putting them together, we gave up and went looking for help.

Luckily, there was a nickel and dime store near us and we hoped there would be something we could use. We looked at hooks and all sorts of tools. Then we split up. Ayana went with Papa, and I went with Mom. Mom and I, though really it was Mom's idea, thought a cat toy that had a stick would be able to get the keys closer to us, but the only problem would be pulling them all the way up. Meanwhile, Ayana and Papa found a backscratcher that had claws!

It seemed like the better option, so we went back to the car. It was too short, so we had to attach the charging cord, which made it really floppy! Mom was able to get one of the claw fingers around the keychain, but she couldn't bring it up. After a few more tries, we decided to go get the cat toy, so Mom went back to the store.

Meanwhile, Papa was fidgeting with the backscratcher. He had this ingenious idea! He asked if I had any tape, and I actually did! So he wrapped the tape on the backscratcher backwards so the sticky side was facing out. He only had one try, otherwise the stickiness would go away, and he actually managed to get the keys close enough to the seat to press the button and unlock the car! These are important life lessons: always have tape with you when you are traveling, and always be resourceful and smart. This knowledge can save your life one day, so use it wisely!
author: zarmina

title: A Day on the Scottish Farm 🐕‍🦺🐑🐂
excerpt: Today we went to this sheepdog demonstration, and it was really cool! As we were driving up, we saw this little puppy coming up the road. It was super cute and I couldn't believe it, it looked just like my dog, Ruby! When we got there and s
body:
Today we went to this sheepdog demonstration, and it was really cool! As we were driving up, we saw this little puppy coming up the road. It was super cute and I couldn't believe it, it looked just like my dog, Ruby!

When we got there and saw all the dogs, there were even more little puppies, like six of them! They were so incredibly cute and adorable, and you could cuddle and pet them as much as you wanted. I held one of the puppies and it was so sweet, and one even crawled right underneath my leg and bit my pants because they were really soft! I just loved it so much.

Once we sat down, the farmer was in the middle of talking, but we were able to catch up quickly. Before showing us how the dogs work, he demonstrated this special trick with his sheep whistle. He took the whistle, which has a little hole in it, held it near the sheep's eye, and moved it back and forth. It kind of hypnotized the sheep so that it fell into a trance and got super calm! When he first pulled the sheep over by its horns, it was trying to ram him and go all over the place, but after the whistle trick, it was completely still. It was insane!

It was so cool to see in real life how the sheepdogs herd up all of the sheep so efficiently. He had different whistles for each of his dogs so they knew exactly when to follow his commands. At one point, one of the dogs started going after a sheep because it is their natural instinct to go in for the kill when they get too excited, but the shepherd knew what was happening and stopped it before it escalated.

While all that was happening, I saw the mother of the puppies nursing them, and it was adorable! All the puppies would gather around her to nurse, and it was so cute. The mother would lick some of the puppies to clean them, and when they were being annoying, she would nip them. It went lick, lick, bite, over and over again! Also, whenever she went somewhere, most of them would follow her. She went over to the creek to dig a hole, and they all came back soaking wet and partially covered in dirt!

Then I even got to watch him shear a sheep! It took him maybe like five minutes to do one. He has 35,000 sheep, and it would cost £5,000 to hire a professional shearer, so he shears all 35,000 sheep himself! He does it so fast and efficiently, and I can totally see why he does it to save so much money, all while chatting and answering our questions the whole time.

After that, we got to feed the cows and sheep. I got to feed a baby cow with a little bottle, and you had to keep a really steady hand! The calf kept wanting more and more milk, even when there wasn't any left.

The farmer answered all my questions and talked about the three Border Collies, which have that pretty white line down their nose and the white collar around their neck. He looked at a picture of Ruby and said, "Yeah, she's definitely a Border Collie mixed with some Australian Shepherd." He said five is a great age for training, but since she is a house pet now, it might not work as well. He also mentioned that by working dog standards, she would be considered an "ugly" dog, not because she is actually ugly, but just because of how her face colors and shape are pattern-wise! I loved this so much, it was just a great experience, and I would totally recommend it if you come to Scotland!
author: zarmina

title: Fun with the Border Collies ,Sheepies, and Cows🐄 🐑 🐕‍🦺
excerpt: Today we were on a car ride to go to this border collie place, but first we decided to eat some food. So we went to this cafe and we got some food. I got a pick and mix, which is like a bunch of foods on a plate. It was not that much, which
body:
Today we were on a car ride to go to this border collie place, but first we decided to eat some food. So we went to this cafe and we got some food. I got a pick and mix, which is like a bunch of foods on a plate. It was not that much, which I like because I don't like very big meals, so it was nice for me. It was tomatoes, bread, and some butter. Zarmina gave me two of her flower petals, so it looked really nice. There were also peppers and carrots.

After that, we went up to the border collie thing. When we were driving up there, we saw this adorable little dog and we were like, "Oh my god, that's so cute, and it looks just like Ruby, our dog!" Ruby is a mix. She's like a border collie and stuff.

We went up and saw all these dogs. The guy wasn't down there yet, so we were waiting. There were all these dogs, and there were also really small dogs that he was letting out of the car. Once we got inside the gate, everybody was petting and picking up all these little puppies, so I decided to do the same. They were so adorable and fluffy. I just can't even explain it. They were so cute!

After I pet them for a while, he started to talk about training the dogs and them herding up sheep. Then he gave us an example and told the older dogs to go and round up the sheep. When they did that, one of the dogs was trying to hunt the sheep, and that wasn't supposed to happen. This happened a couple of times where two sheep jumped over the fence into somewhere else. We're not sure if he noticed, but I'm pretty sure that they were allowed to do it because he didn't do anything.

Then he grabbed a sheep by its horns and pulled it over because it needed to be sheared. He did this thing with the whistle where it calmed down the sheep when he swung it in front of its eyes. Then he cut the sheep's wool off and let it go. A few other people like me also cut off the wool.

At the end, we went over and I, along with some other people, fed the cow and some sheep some milk. At the very end, he gave all the kids postcards. I stayed till the very end because I was hugging this one baby dog, and he told us that he was only going to keep one dog. I was like, "Can I adopt it?" It was so cute. I wanted to take it back with me, but we couldn't, and we had to leave.

But then, he was really kind, so he gave Zarmina and me a whistle for free. I could not believe it. I was so happy. If you are in Scotland, it was so much fun for me, I bet it would be for you too!
author: ayana

title: A Cold-Blooded Murder! 🐸😭😭
excerpt: A cold-blooded murder.  That's what I am! 😭😭😭😭😭 Let's start at the beginning. Today I was on this lovely trail and saw a frog. I stopped to gush over how cute it was, and then I saw another and another. There were so many! I kept on st
body:
A cold-blooded murder.

That's what I am! 😭😭😭😭😭

Let's start at the beginning. Today I was on this lovely trail and saw a frog. I stopped to gush over how cute it was, and then I saw another and another. There were so many! I kept on stopping to say hi because they were adorable. At this rate, a walk that would take one hour was going to take us thirteen! Eventually, I saw them so much that it wasn't as exciting.

Then on the side of the trail, I saw this fluorescent beetle with blues, greens, and purples. It was on its back, so we decided to turn it over with a stick and come back later to see if it made it to wherever it was lumbering off to.

As we were walking, I kept an eye out for frogs, and I almost stepped on one like thirty times! I knew my luck was running out, and I just hoped that I wouldn't be there when it did. The next second, I was squishing a frog! Everything happened so fast. I was walking and keeping an eye out for frogs. I saw a few near my shoes and didn't think much of it, so when I took a step, a frog jumped right under my shoe!

I immediately turned around. There was a pile of jelly-ish substance. It had two feet at the end of where I stretched it out, and the rest of the body was squished upward. I don't know if the frog went under my foot by mistake or if it was suicide!

I feel so bad! How could I be so mean? I can just imagine its tombstone: RIP Bobby (that's what I named it), squished by a human. I can imagine its whole family weeping! 😭 I can imagine all the frogs coming together into one giant frog and then squishing me while I cross a crosswalk! I can't die like that! The poor squished frog! 😭

Although, honestly, it could have just been poop.
author: zarmina

title: The Jacobite (Harry Potter Train): An Exciting Experience 🛤
excerpt: Today we were going to see the Jacobite, which is the Harry Potter train! We had to get in our car early, and I didn't really get to do anything because we ended up having to wait for another 20 minutes, even though we were trying to get th
body:
Today we were going to see the Jacobite, which is the Harry Potter train! We had to get in our car early, and I didn't really get to do anything because we ended up having to wait for another 20 minutes, even though we were trying to get there 20 minutes early.

Anyway, as we were driving up, we saw loads of cars in the parking lots, which were all closed. I mean, obviously nobody is going to move when they are waiting to see the Harry Potter train go over the Viaduct! So we were about to turn around, but Mom asked the parking attendant if there was any parking left anywhere. She said, "Um, I don't think so, but there might be space behind that truck." Then she realized there was actually a spot open right behind it, so we were able to park! When we paid the £5 for parking, it turned out that it also came with a free pass to go to the museum, so it was a total win-win!

It was a 30 minute walk along the trail to get to the viaduct. On the way back, it felt way more uphill than it did on the way there. Walking to the train felt pretty downhill, but it didn't feel like a steep downhill either, so that was a little weird.

Anyway, when we got there, we found a nice spot away from everybody where there were only two other people. Papa went to go closer to the viaduct, where there were like 30 million people around him! I didn't even notice the train was coming at first, but once it appeared, I quickly started videoing it. In the middle of the video, I took a quick photo with Ayana, and then went right back to recording the rest of it. The Harry Potter train looked so cool with all the smoke and steam billowing out of it! Papa was so close that he could even see the conductor waving his hand!

When we walked back, we saw a mini Jacobite train, which was a super cute miniature version of the real steam train. Soon after, I started smelling fish and chips as we got near this restaurant that was actually built inside an old train car, which was so cool! I had the best fish and chips. It had the absolute right amount of crunch and was really soft on the inside. The fries were delectable! They were fluffy on the inside, crispy on the outside, sprinkled with salt, and the ketchup gave them such a great pop of flavor. The salad was really good, too, and I loved the dressing with the tomatoes all mixed together.

Then we went to the museum and met these German folks who had the cutest dog ever! They travel everywhere with their dog, and they told us all about this special travel airline just for dogs. Hearing about that made me miss Ruby so much, but that's okay. Overall, I had so much fun today, even with almost missing the train!
author: zarmina

title: The Beautiful Hike 🏞🪻

Today we went on a hike around this loch, and it was really pretty! The scenery would sometimes be planted trees far and wide as far as the eye can see, though I don't know if they are being used for logging or if they are to repopulate the trees here in the Highlands.

Then we saw open fields with these pretty purple flowers covering them. There were a few native trees scattered around, but the scenery was absolutely beautiful! We also saw reeds that were covering a marshy area, and they were taller than me! You would look all around, and that is all you would see. The different scenery was all very pretty, and I loved it!
author: zarmina

title: Grass Sledding Fun! 🛷
excerpt: Today we went grass sledding for Mom's birthday! I was pulling this cart with wheels up a hill, getting dragged down, but I finally made it to the top. I was scared but excited to go down the hill. It was really cramped inside the cart, but
body:
Today we went grass sledding for Mom's birthday! I was pulling this cart with wheels up a hill, getting dragged down, but I finally made it to the top.

I was scared but excited to go down the hill. It was really cramped inside the cart, but I managed to squeeze in. Once I started rolling down, it was terrifying, almost like I was about to tip over, but luckily that never happened! I loved the way the wind blew my hair away from my face (non-majestically!) as I picked up speed. I loved how the rush of excitement and giddiness passed right through me. When I came to a stop, I got up and out of the cart, flipping my hair because of course it looked dreadful!

It was so fun seeing other people go down the hill, too. Ayana looked like she had fun, too. She kept going up and down, up and down. But she was scared to go too fast and didn't let me push her really far and fast, which was sad. Anyway, it was so much fun!

When Mom went, she was really cramped, so it hurt her hips, and she didn't go again. There was also this woman who decided to go because of my mom. When she was going down the hill, she drifted a little too far to the left where there was this thistle patch, and she ran right into the thistles! Luckily, she wasn't hurt at all.

When Papa went, he went again and again and again! He encouraged this other dad to come and go down the hill, and that dad had the funniest expression on his face. His hair was whipping around in his face, his mouth was halfway open, and his eyes had a look of terror and excitement all muddled together. It was hilarious! One time Papa got out on the hill and was doing all these moves with his arms, and when he raised his arm in the middle of going down, he swerved all the way to the left, which was so funny. Overall, it was such an awesome day and so much fun!
author: zarmina

title: The Walk To Hagrid's Hut 🛖
excerpt: Today we went on a hike! It was beautiful with all the cute, picturesque flowers lining the path. We even saw some Highland cows doing what they do best, eating! They definitely need all those calories, since an adult Highland cow eats arou
body:
Today we went on a hike! It was beautiful with all the cute, picturesque flowers lining the path. We even saw some Highland cows doing what they do best, eating! They definitely need all those calories, since an adult Highland cow eats around 70 to 150 pounds of grass every single day just to stay fueled up and keep their warm double coats!

We kept on going, with me daydreaming, Mom doing photography, Papa talking, and Ayana sitting and posing for Mom. It was insanely pretty and the weather was perfect. I bathed in sunlight and enjoyed the hike. We were walking up this steep hill to get to the scene where Hagrid's hut was filmed in the third movie.

As I was walking up this muddy trail because of all the rain in the past week, I put my foot on a loose rock. I fell straight into the mud! Luckily my hand prevented my hair and the rest of my body from getting coated in mud, even though I heard that mud makes your skin softer, which is a plus. Anyway, then we saw the scene where Hagrid's hut was created. It was so cool! I would totally recommend going, but not the falling part though!

Then we went to grab some food after our long hike. I got this sandwich with cheese, tomatoes, and a sauce to bring it all together. The tomatoes gave it a crunch, and the white bread dialed down the flavors nicely. The sauce gave it a pop of taste, and the cheese gave it a nice touch. It was probably the best sandwich I've ever had!

Anyway, I had loads of fun experiences and yummy food. It is great here in Scotland, and I'm especially loving the views and the food!
author: zarmina

title: The Attack of the of the Bugs: Part 2 🐝
excerpt: Today, when I was walking on this beautiful hike with cute purple flowers minding my own business, a bee flew right at my head! Like, rude! Really, the parenting of the queen bee has gone downhill quite a bit. Anyway, since I wasn't expect
body:
Today, when I was walking on this beautiful hike with cute purple flowers minding my own business, a bee flew right at my head! Like, rude! Really, the parenting of the queen bee has gone downhill quite a bit.

Anyway, since I wasn't expecting this behavior from bees, I jumped back and gave an unflattering screech! So after this, I hope that my letter will reach the queen bee so that she can do some better parenting.

Also, since now I had an excuse to flip my hair in case the bee was in my hair, so of course I did a few hundred hair flips! So now I'm continuing my hike to Hagrid's hut. Hopefully the next generation of bees are better behaved!
author: zarmina

title: The adventures inside the hike 🥾
excerpt: Today, we went on a hike to this amazing castle. When we got there, I saw this sign that said, "Warning: Do not go near or in the castle. It's dangerous," and stuff like that. I looked at the sign and I was like, "Yeah, right."
body:
Today, we went on a hike to this amazing castle. When we got there, I saw this sign that said, "Warning: Do not go near or in the castle. It's dangerous," and stuff like that. I looked at the sign and I was like, "Yeah, right." Once we walked up to the castle, I was looking around, and I was the first one there, and I found an entrance. So, I went inside. It was a castle ruin, so I just walked through this little space. Once I walked in, I looked around for a bit. I saw where Zarmina was sitting and Mom was taking a photo. I found an easier way to get up. I found all these little cool areas.

Then I came out because Puppy and Mummy were starting to arrive, and Dan was too. Puppy started climbing up the castle ruins, and I was like, "Oh, I should follow him. That looks fun." I followed him, and there was this really beautiful green scenery with plants everywhere. It was so pretty at the top of the castle. Zarmina and I were searching everywhere, looking around. We went under, and we saw this little place. Dan came up from a different way, and I went down and came up. It was really fun. I even saw where the dungeons might have been, or like a dung room or something.

We saw two graves, and there was a mausoleum next to it. It was also broken down. Puppy first discovered that there was a miniature mouse inside of it. It was so adorable. It was shivering, probably afraid, but it might have also been cold, because Scotland is very cold. Puppy gave it a leaf, but it was so cute. It was so fuzzy. It was so warm, and I don't think it was even scared of us. Yeah, I don't think it was scared of us because it wasn't running away or anything.

More people came, and they were also checking out the castle. We told them to go and check out the cute little mouse. They checked it out, and then more people came, and they also checked out the mouse. This one woman came up, and she put her hands down. She was like, "Oh, it might be sick," because it was shivering, and like, "Mice don't usually do this." It didn't even try to escape when I picked it up. They were like some animal experts, so they were going to see if they could help the mouse.

I checked it out for a little bit more, and we walked around. When we were walking down this little path to go back to the mausoleum, because we just went on a tiny little walk, Zarmina pricked her finger, and it caused the smallest cut possible. She dramatically overreacted. After that catastrophe, we walked a little bit more and went down this path. We thought the hike would be over soon because it was going to rain eventually.

We saw all these trees and stuff, and there was this little area where there was a river and sand, so it was kind of like a beach, but not really. We checked that out, and near there, there was some grass and a few trees, and there were sheep. The sheep were so adorable, but the trail was covered in sheep poop. It was really fun to see the sheepies!

After Puppy took a few photos, we walked a little bit more to a big field. Puppy was like, "Oh, we should go down this path," and we went down that path. It was a little bit smaller than the other path that we were thinking of going on, but it was okay. Once we followed that path, it took an abrupt stop. There were sheepies under the tree, and we took a little photos, but we knew that it was the wrong path and we had to go back to the other path. We just walked through all the grass-like things, and then we finally found the right path.

On the path, there was this gate that was completely useless. It was in the middle of the road, and you could literally just walk around it. But we decided to open the gate and go through, and we were like, "Quickly, quickly, we don't want to let the sheepies out!" We were like, "Ha ha ha," because we were trying to make a joke out of it since you could just go around it.

We got finished soon and ate in the car. It started to drizzle after we got back, which is good that we got there in time. If you're in Edinburgh, you should definitely check out that castle. The walk was pretty fun!
author: ayana

title: Scooty and the Bloodthursty Tick 🪳
